title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection with hysteresis and rollout guards
author: Samir Patel
description: Context: Our performance canary system has reliably detected regressions, but we continue to see noisy aborts driven by transient spikes and infra jitter. This PR introduces two improvements: (1) hysteresis in the detector to require sustained regressions before triggering a canary abort and (2) stronger rollout guards that correlate latency/throughput signals with infra-level anomalies to avoid false positives. Summary of changes: - Add adaptive smoothing and hysteresis windows for latency and throughput detectors (configurable by rollout policy). - Implement correlation checks between canary metric regressions and infra signals (node CPU, GPU utilization, queue length, pod restarts). - Add a new 'grace period' phase to the canary state machine: initial-eval -> grace -> stable; aborts are only allowed after grace unless severity threshold reached. - Introduce per-customer and per-model sensitivity profiles (conservative/default/aggressive) for Retail and Enterprise tiers. - New dashboard panels and trace tags to aid debugging (canary_id, window_size, hysteresis_count). - Add integration tests that simulate transient spikes and sustained regressions. Motivation: reduce customer impact from noisy auto-rollbacks while keeping detection sensitive to real regressions. We want fast detection for high-severity regressions but fewer false aborts when the root cause is infra or ephemeral load. Compatibility: Fully backward compatible; defaults preserve current behavior (default sensitivity == previous behavior). Operators can opt-in to more aggressive detection via rollout policy. Checklist: - [x] Detector algorithm implementation - [x] Rollout guard infra correlation - [x] Config + rollout policy knobs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Metrics + dashboard updates - [x] Documentation (console + runbook) Risk notes: The main risk is mis-tuning hysteresis that delays detection for real regressions; mitigated by conservative default and Linear task ENG-5421 for follow-up tuning. Rollout: squash merge to main after approvals; feature gated behind rollout.policies.canary_hysteresis flag.

Diego Martinez: The correlation check looks good but add unit tests covering missing infra data (should be tolerant).

Priya Nair: How does this interact with canary batch sizes? If batching changes throughput distribution might look like regression.
Samir Patel: We tie effective window to observed qps and batch size; added a note in the runbook and a small adjustment to smoothing to account for batching variance.

release_notes: Improved canary auto-detection with hysteresis and rollout guards: reduces false-positive canary aborts by requiring sustained regressions and correlating with infra signals. Operators can tune sensitivity via rollout policies. Includes dashboards and tests.
notes_for_release: Flag-gated behind rollout.policies.canary_hysteresis. Recommend enabling in staging and monitoring for 48h before enabling in prod for high-sensitivity models.
risk_mitigation: Default sensitivity preserves existing behavior. Canaries will only abort after grace period unless severity threshold is met. Rollback path unchanged; manual abort still available.
